reviews.text: Love this app!

reviews.title: Simple and does what it says it’ll do.
reviews.text: Every other calorie tracking app or fitness app over complicates everything. This app takes formulas and uses the data you put in to actually curate a plan for you. I said I wanted to lose 2 lbs a week and it has me doing exactly that. And maybe that isn’t so special but what is special is the fact that this app doesn’t shove its subscription version down your throat. Yes it’ll pop up every couple days or so. But, to me it actually does seem worth it but the app works perfectly fine without paying a cent. No ads either. If you’re actually serious about your diet and cutting/bulking is something you do frequently and need real data that updates in real time based on your progress get this app.

reviews.title: Nah
reviews.text:
Wanted to like this app! Seemed to have great potential! 
2 problems: seeing any macros is behind a paywall, which I don’t care much for the fancy upgrades, but seeing how much protein I’ve consumed is pretty necessary. 
Plus the food I kept inputting was higher calories than the container itself said aka my non fat Greek yogurt was 40 calories more than it actually was. 
If these were fixed it’d be a great app!

reviews.title: Questionable calorie content data
reviews.text:
Definitely helpful but there are multiple entries for the calories in a food which makes it difficult to know which is accurate. I even found one for “fried chicken and mashed protesters”. 😂
Make one wonder who’s editing this thing. It did help me reach my goal though.

reviews.title: Great info/unfortunate app
reviews.text: This app provides a ton of helpful info and good advice. However the diet tracking portion of the app is like communicating with someone who’s never heard of food. It’s impossible to actually track accurate intake because it doesn’t have reasonable selections. If the app were improved I would definitely try the service again!

reviews.title: Add micronutrients and ai is wildly inaccurate
reviews.text: The app is really nice and I like that there’s more nuance to the calorie goals opposed to other apps. But for such a Hefty subscription price I’m extremely disappointed to not be able to see micronutrients or even fiber intake. These things are just as important to nutrition and true health as macronutrients. I also added a chick fil a kale crunch salad and the ai calculated it to be 400 calories but it’s actually 170. The grilled nuggets were more accurate calorically but the macros were very off. About a 8 gram protein difference. They say to check the info but don’t give you a way to edit it and their feature for adding calories without a label doesn’t allow you to track macros.

reviews.title: Good for pure calorie tracking
reviews.text:
The app works well for purely calorie tracking and has a cool ai integration, although it’s not always accurate. Compared to other apps I would say this one falls short in several ways. First, there is no way I could find to input foods with macros that I can’t find in the database. So I can either just purely track the calories or try to find a similar food with incorrect macros. When trying for a specific daily protein intake, this can be pretty annoying. 

Saving meals or foods is not intuitive. The bar scanning feature is nice but often the data base can’t find the food or barcode. There is no integration between smart calorie trackers and the app. I know the app attempts to calculate metabolic rate and daily caloric need over time with weight loss but it would be nice to see what days more calories were burned and how that effected by caloric intake and macro break down. It also would more accurately track the metabolic rate.

I think with some tweaks the app could work great but compared to something like HitMeal for iOS, it falls well short.

reviews.title: Just be in calorie deficit
reviews.text: This app works great for tracking calories. It’s got an AI search for foods. It’s simple to lose weight. Be in a calorie deficit, don’t cheat, don’t lie to yourself. You’re going to be hungry. You get used to it. You got this. Try and get healthy foods, but in a pinch; you don’t need them. Just track your calories
